recent_cases.parties: Ms Judith Bruce v Community Based Support Limited
recent_cases.ai_summary: Ms Bruce was dismissed by Community Based Support Limited when her Service Delivery Coordinator (Social Hubs) role was made redundant following discontinuation of NDIS services. The FWC found the employer no longer required the job to be performed but that it failed to comply with its enterprise agreement obligation to consult about the redundancy, including discussing the likely effect of the change on the employee. The genuine redundancy objection was therefore dismissed and the matter will be listed for further directions.

recent_cases.parties: Mining and Energy Union (301V) v Anglo Coal (Moranbah North Management) Pty Ltd
recent_cases.ai_summary: The MEU challenged a Level 2 disciplinary warning issued to Mr Jamieson for arriving late to a safety briefing after deliberately booking a flight he knew would make him late. The Commission found significant procedural flaws and that the Level 2 warning was unreasonable, but that a lesser penalty was open. It reduced the warning to a Level 1 warning effective from 24 March 2025.

recent_cases.parties: Federation University Australia T/A Federation University Australia v National Tertiary Education Industry Union (283V)
recent_cases.ai_summary: Federation University applied under s.739 to resolve a dispute with the NTEU over the proposed Academic Workload Model for its Institute of Health and Wellbeing under clause 35 of the enterprise agreement. The Commission found the Academic Workload Committee had not discharged its responsibilities and that the University had not complied with consultation requirements, so the model as proposed could not proceed. The Commission answered the parties' questions, holding any validly developed and endorsed AWM should apply from the start of the academic year following endorsement, and made recommendations for consultation and a staff ballot.

recent_cases.parties: Mr Adrian Clay v Peninsula Directional Drilling Pty Ltd
recent_cases.ai_summary: Mr Clay, employed as General Manager at Peninsula Directional Drilling, applied for an unfair dismissal remedy. Peninsula objected that he was not protected from unfair dismissal because no modern award or enterprise agreement covered him and his guaranteed annual earnings of $235,000 exceeded the high-income threshold. Applying the principal purpose test, the Commission found his role was primarily running the business rather than clerical work, upheld the jurisdictional objection, and dismissed the application.

recent_cases.parties: Boi v Aldi Foods Pty Ltd
recent_cases.ai_summary: The Federal Court approved a settlement of a representative proceeding brought by current and former ALDI employees for unpaid work in contravention of s 50 of the Fair Work Act, together with a parallel union penalty proceeding. The settlement, valued at approximately $55.2 million including interest and prior voluntary payments, was found fair and reasonable with no deductions for legal costs or funder commission, and ALDI appointed scheme administrator. Justice McElwaine also found the distribution methodology fair and reasonable and rejected the single objection.
